tieu_de: Neptune transit through the 7th house: seeing your partner through the fog
mo: Is my partner hiding something from me?
Can a relationship that starts under this transit last?
Should I be careful with business partnerships now?

Relationships always involve a bit of projection. We see partly who someone is and partly who we hope they are. When O Neptune moves into your 7th house, that ratio shifts toward hope, and the task of the next several years is learning to see the people closest to you more truly.
It can be deeply romantic. It can also be confusing. Often it is both, sometimes in the same week.

doan: The 7th house covers committed relationships: marriage, long-term partners, business partners, contracts, and open rivals. It is the house of the significant other. Neptune softens edges, raises empathy, and invites idealisation.

The library reading describes close bonds becoming hard to read. You or your partner may idealise, misunderstand, or fail to see each other's real nature. New relationships deserve time to show whether the feeling is genuine or mostly expectation. Business and contractual partnerships need careful checking for unclear terms, and alcohol or other stimulants can be a source of avoidable trouble.
Planet Neptune Rules Pisces Imagination, intuition, spirituality

A partner seems to drift, emotionally or physically, and you cannot name exactly why. Or you are the one drifting, longing for a closeness you cannot find at home. New people arrive who feel like rescuers, or who seem to need rescuing.
In business, a partner may be vague about money or commitments. A contract has a clause nobody explained. A collaborator promises more than they deliver.
There is also real tenderness available. Couples sometimes become more compassionate, more spiritual together, or more forgiving of old hurts.

Neptune in the 7th can take a relationship past bargaining and into genuine compassion. You learn to love someone including their flaws, and to accept love that is not perfect. Shared creative or spiritual interests can become a strong bond.
This transit also teaches discernment. By the end of it, most people are far better at telling the difference between a real connection and a beautiful fantasy.

Idealisation and deception are the big themes. That can mean staying with someone because of who they might become, overlooking dishonesty, or entering a relationship to save someone. It can also mean you are less than honest yourself, softening truths to avoid conflict.
Unclear agreements in business partnerships are another risk. And if either partner leans on alcohol or other substances to cope, problems can grow quietly.

Neptune stays in a sign for about 14 years, and a transit through a house is on a similar order, though your 7th house may be larger or smaller depending on house system and birth latitude. The most significant relationship moments often arrive when Neptune crosses your Descendant or aspects Venus.
Slow down new commitments. Let a relationship go through seasons before you marry, move in, or mix finances. Watch what the person does over time, not only what they say.
Speak plainly in existing relationships. Neptune rewards gentle honesty. Name what you need, ask what your partner needs, and check assumptions out loud.
Read every partnership agreement carefully. In business, get roles, money, and exit terms in writing. If someone resists clarity, that tells you something.
Notice the rescue impulse. Compassion is good; taking responsibility for another adult's life is not sustainable. Support, but do not carry.
Be mindful with alcohol and other stimulants, particularly in shared social life. Keep the relationship's good times clear-headed.

Not necessarily. Neptune in the 7th makes relationships feel vague, and that can come from distance, stress, or unspoken feelings rather than lies. If something feels off, ask directly and kindly, and pay attention to patterns over time rather than single moments.
Yes. Many do, especially when both people take their time and stay honest. The relationships that struggle are usually those built quickly on a fantasy that never meets real life.
Yes. Check terms, roles, and money flow carefully, and get independent advice on anything significant. Clear agreements protect friendship as much as finances.
